sam_support: hey @lee_eng — customer seeing intermittent 403 during streaming after token rotation. They gave a curl but we couldn't repro. request id: r-8f3a2ef2. Happened ~2026-03-12T18:22Z in us-west-2. Can we get a minimal curl checklist to validate?

lee_eng: thanks. a few quick Qs: are they hitting a proxy? using ephemeral tokens from our rotation service? do they observe failure immediately after rotation or after some time into the stream?

sam_support: proxy (company proxy) yes. they say it fails ~30s after stream start, sometimes immediately. token rotation is every 60s for this client. customer supplied this curl (token masked):

sam_support: ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-rl"
```

anya_prod: :eyes: probable race between token refresh and long-lived connection. we should capture full request/response headers and a byte-level trace to see if a 401/403 is injected by proxy or our edge when rotation happens.

lee_eng: checklist for reproducer (short):
1) reproduce with same network path (if behind proxy, try via that proxy or VPN).
2) run curl with --http1.1 and --no-buffer so SSE isn't buffered: `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer ...`
3) include `-i` to print response headers.
4) use `--trace-ascii /tmp/trace-ascii.log` to capture handshake + TLS details.
5) use `-H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` and keep a secondary script that rotates the token at 60s to mimic customer rotation.
6) capture X-Request-Id / X-Trace-Id from response headers. we log those server-side.

lee_eng: sample command we ask them to run (mask tokens when sharing):
```
curl -i -N --http1.1 --no-buffer \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>" \
  --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.log \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-rl"
```

lee_eng: while it's running, if it fails paste top-of-trace.log and the response headers. also note the precise clock time so we can map to edge logs. if they can't share trace, ask for `grep -n "HTTP/1.1" /tmp/trace.log | tail -n 50` and the chunk that contains the 403.

sam_support: got it. should we ask them to explicitly add `Connection: keep-alive` header?

lee_eng: not necessary usually, but can try if proxy manipulates connection state. also try adding `-H "TE: trailers"` to match some proxies. key thing: capture pre-rotation success response headers and post-rotation 403 headers. post them here.

anya_prod: remember to ask for the client side token refresh logs (time of refresh) and proxy access logs (if available). we can correlate request-id with our edge logs.

sam_support: I'll send them the command + checklist. will ask them to redact tokens and upload /tmp/trace.log and headers to our secure upload (support bucket).

infra-bot: deploy/edge-logging: new log retention policy applied to streams-edge in us-west-2 — search by X-Request-Id will be available for last 48h.

lee_eng: if we still can't repro, next step is to run a local token-rotation harness: small script that opens curl then rotates token via separate process at 60s to try to hit the exact timing. I can paste a tiny node/python harness if needed.

sam_support: perfect. customer asked for low-friction steps, I'll start with the single curl + trace approach and ask them to upload. will follow up with the harness if they can't repro locally. :thumbsup:

lee_eng: thanks — ping me with the upload link (and the X-Request-Id). we'll correlate and triage.
